decisive_items: Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105)
diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk
response.rationale: The constellation of hypopituitarism, pituitary/stalk swelling, elevated IgG4, and suspected systemic IgG4-related disease strongly favors IgG4-related hypophysitis over lymphocytic hypophysitis, which would not explain the IgG4 elevation and systemic findings.

rejected.why: Sinus mucosal thickening and a lung nodule are nonspecific; there is no ANCA, cavitary lung disease, glomerulonephritis, or sinonasal destructive pattern to support granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
Lymphocytic hypophysitis shares pituitary/stalk swelling and hypopituitarism, but it does not account for the markedly elevated IgG4 and suspected systemic IgG4-related disease.

The 7-mm pituitary mass could be present in inflammatory disease; however, the diffuse stalk/pituitary swelling, hypopituitarism, and IgG4 elevation favor an inflammatory IgG4-related process over sellar lymphoma.
